title: The influence of physical activity-related health competence on the habitual physical activity of patients with post-COVID
summary:
Physical activity is considered a protective factor against both SARS-CoV-2 infection and severe COVID-19. In addition, physical inactivity is a risk factor for long-lasting symptoms, which are classified as post-COVID if they persist for more than 12 weeks. In the current S1 guideline Long-/Post-COVID, health-promoting physical activity is recommended as a preventive and rehabilitative treatment strategy in accordance with WHO guidelines. The implementation of a physically active lifestyle within the individual's exercise tolerance can play a central role in the long-term improvement of biopsychosocial health and the maintenance or recovery of work ability in post-COVID patients. The current research project aims to identify biopsychosocial parameters that have a beneficial or inhibitory influence on the activity behaviour of post-COVID patients. Of particular interest is the holistic concept of physical activity related health competence.
With the help of digital assessment methods for activity analysis in everyday life and in interaction with biopsychosocial factors, evidence-based guidelines for targeted behavioural prevention measures for post-COVID patients in aftercare can be derived.

interventions.name: At each of the four measurement points, participants are first asked to complete a questionnaire on their socio-demographic data, COVID-19/post-COVID history, physical activity related health literacy, biopsychosocial factors, mental health and ability to work. They then wear a motion sensor for 24h

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The participants are at least 18 years old.
The participants are in the post-acute phase (>12 weeks after acute infection) with persistent post-COVID symptoms.
The participants have a medically confirmed post-COVID (U09.9 or U08.9 or U10.9).
The participants take part in the study voluntarily.
Exclusion criteria:
Severe cardiovascular, respiratory, neurological or musculoskeletal disease and mental (e.g. severe depression) or neurocognitive (e.g. dementia) diagnosis prior to COVID-19.
